proposals.before: In the third year of Tiancheng (562), he was promoted to advising officer of the northern expedition and concurrently supervisor of the court of ceremonial rites.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianjia (562), he was promoted to advising officer of the northern expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.reason: Chinese 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng; 廷尉監 is a Judicial Review post, not ceremonial rites.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tiancheng, he was promoted to advising officer of the Northern Expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Ceremonial Rites.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianjia, he was promoted to advising officer of the Northern Expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.reason: Same errors as idiomatic: era name and office mistranslated.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Zhide (586) he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these suppress former canons.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Zhide (586) he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these are indeed the former canons.
proposals.reason: 抑乃前典 means 'these are indeed former canons,' not 'suppress.'

decisions.reason: s0051 has 天嘉三年 and 廷尉監; Tiancheng and ceremonial rites misread the Chen era name and the judicial office, and the proposed idiomatic replacement is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天嘉三年，遷征北諮議參軍，兼廷尉監。

decisions.reason: Same unit: 天嘉 is Tianjia and 廷尉監 is the Court of Judicial Review supervisorship, not ceremonial rites; the proposed literal replacement matches the Chinese.
In the edict clause 抑乃前典, 抑乃 affirms that coffin-closing and posthumous titles are indeed the former canons; reading 抑 as 'suppress' reverses the sense, and the proposed wording restores it.
